## About Me

I study how climate extremes and disturbance affect forest growth and carbon storage, with a focus on the resilience of eastern U.S. temperate forests as carbon sinks.

My dissertation examines how extreme heat, atmospheric drought, and non-lethal tree damage affect woody productivity, and whether canopy carbon uptake continues to translate into long-lived woody biomass under increasing climate stress.

My research integrates long-term forest monitoring, dendrometer measurements, tree-ring analyses, flux-tower observations, and remote sensing.

## Research Interests

- Forest responses to climate extremes
- Ecosystem carbon cycling and forest carbon sinks
- Tree growth and woody biomass accumulation
- Carbon uptake–growth decoupling
- Forest resilience and disturbance
